items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Then we had a fellow, his name was Freddie Blackburn.

ctx.x: So, then we had another -- they had a girl and her name was Gertie Waters. She could read all the music, couldn't do some of the jazz, but she would play those chords for you. And Kurzie was a beautiful saxophone player. Beautiful fellow.

Then we had a fellow, his name was Freddie Blackburn. his father was West Indian, his mother French Now, Freddie was a Canadian, he was Canadian, but -- this poor boy, there was an awful calamity in his life.

It seems that he had six sisters and he himself, I think what I am hearing, is that his father, when they came of age to understand, they were trying to make fun of the Metis-- father because him being black and they were being -/- mixed and everything, they would make fun of him.
